question: Can Brightwave Logistics pay a tax-free home-office allowance to Belgian-employed staff living in France who work from home 2 days a week?

transcript.text: Hi, it's Nadia from Brightwave Logistics in Liège. Fourteen of our planners live in France and now work from home two days a week. Can we keep paying them the monthly home-office allowance tax-free? And does it change anything else in their payroll?
Good question. I'll double-check the cross-border rules and call you back.

Reading the Belgian telework policy and cross-border guidance

extracts.title: Policy — Home-office allowance (Belgium)
extracts.path: KB › Legal & Compliance BE › Telework › HOA-policy-2026
extracts.excerpt: The monthly home-office allowance can be paid free of tax and social contributions when telework is structural (at least 1 day per week, documented in a telework agreement) and the amount stays within the published ceiling.

flags.text: Official policy, owner assigned, reviewed March 2026
Written for Belgian residents; non-residents not mentioned

extracts.title: Guideline — Cross-border employees France–Belgium
extracts.excerpt: Days worked from home in the country of residence may count as work performed abroad. Above the tolerated number of days, part of the salary may become taxable in France. Social-security affiliation (A1) must be reviewed if telework exceeds 25%.

flags.text: 5 years old; post-2022 telework agreements are not reflected
The author has left and no owner is assigned

groups.assessment: Wrong country, so it does not apply

extracts.title: Procedure — Thuiswerkvergoeding (NL)
extracts.excerpt: The daily home-working allowance is paid untaxed per registered home-working day, via the work-related costs scheme.

flags.text: Dutch rules, not applicable to a Belgian employer

signals.text: The Teams message (E3) says “no issue”, while the 2021 guideline (E4) says telework days may shift taxation to France.
The most relevant document (E4) has no owner since its author left in 2023.
E4 is 5 years old; cross-border telework rules have changed since.
One result (E5) is Dutch and was excluded from the answer.

answer.text: The Belgian policy allows a tax-free home-office allowance for structural telework, but it was written for Belgian residents and explicitly refers cross-border cases to International Mobility. The only cross-border source is from 2021 and unowned; it warns that telework days in France may shift part of the taxation and affect social security. A recent Teams message says “no issue”, but it is informal and concerns another client.
answer.indicative: Likely: the allowance itself can stay, but the 2 telework days in France may change tax and social-security treatment. This is unconfirmed.

keyPoints.text: The Belgian policy (2026, owned) confirms the allowance for structural telework.
Conflict: the Teams claim contradicts the cross-border guideline.
The cross-border guideline is 5 years old and has no owner.
A1 social-security certificate may need review (2 of 5 days = 40% telework).

answer.gap: Confirm the current France–Belgium rules on telework days for cross-border employees, and whether the allowance and A1 affiliation remain unchanged for Brightwave's 14 employees.
